# CXNM - Standard - WIN - D - Audit Policy Enforcement

Makes the advanced audit settings take precedence over the old category settings, so that the baseline's audit policy actually determines what is logged.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | All Devices |
| Source | CIS v4 Windows 11 L1 and the Microsoft Security Baseline — setting taken from IntuneAdmin's NIS2 profile, value verified against the settings catalog definition. |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Audit_Policy_Enforcement.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Audit_Policy_Enforcement.json) |

> One setting, but the cheapest of the whole set: it adds nothing itself and only ensures that what is already there actually applies. After deployment, run `auditpol /get /category:*` on a test device and compare with the baseline policy. In addition, OneSettings auditing is turned on: Windows records when it fetches configuration from the OneSettings service. Without that trail, a change coming from there cannot be seen afterwards.

## Standards

| Framework | Controls |
|---|---|
| ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | A.8.15 Logging<br>A.8.16 Monitoring activities |
| NIS2 art. 21(2) | art. 21(2)(b) incident handling |
| CIS Controls v8.1 | 8.2 Collect Audit Logs<br>8.5 Collect Detailed Audit Logs |
| NIST CSF 2.0 | PR.PS-04 |

What this means per standard and what is needed organisationally alongside it: [COMPLIANCE.en.md](../../../docs/COMPLIANCE.en.md).
